title: Illustrative example — threshold-based replenishment in a fictional inventory system

source_system.name: Synthetic threshold-based inventory controller
source_system.original_context: A fictional control-system example created only to demonstrate record structure; it is not a claim about a real product or historical system.
source_system.original_function: Maintain a minimum stock of a shared resource while avoiding unnecessary replenishment.
source_system.mechanism_description: The controller observes a stock level, compares it with a threshold that accounts for replenishment delay, and triggers a replenishment action when the threshold is crossed.
source_system.feedback_and_failure: The example assumes repeated measurement and an alert for failed replenishment; both are hypothetical and require specification.

target_problem.problem_statement: A shared workshop wants to reduce tool-stock shortages without over-ordering consumables.
target_problem.target_function: Maintain sufficient shared consumables under variable demand.
target_problem.context: A synthetic design exercise for a small workshop.
constraints: Demand can spike before restocking arrives.
The system must avoid unnecessary orders.

relationship_mappings.source_relationship: A measured stock level is compared with a threshold that accounts for replenishment delay; crossing the threshold triggers replenishment.
relationship_mappings.target_correspondence: A workshop tracks consumable inventory and triggers a restock request before expected demand exhausts the available stock.
relationship_mappings.explanation: The threshold-and-feedback relationship maps, but demand prediction, supplier reliability, human approval, and cost constraints require separate analysis.

abstracted_principle: Use a measured state, a context-sensitive threshold, and feedback to trigger a corrective action before a constrained resource reaches an unacceptable level.
transfer_hypothesis: If a workshop models consumption rate and replenishment delay, a context-sensitive reorder threshold may reduce stockouts without materially increasing excess inventory; this is an untested hypothesis.
mismatch_analysis: A workshop has human purchasing behavior and supplier variability not represented in the fictional controller.
The synthetic example does not establish an optimal reorder point or predict real demand.
failure_modes: Incorrect demand estimates trigger premature or late orders.
A supplier delay exceeds the assumed replenishment window.
Duplicate orders occur after repeated threshold alerts.

test_plan.smallest_test: Replay a small synthetic demand series using the proposed threshold rule and compare it with fixed periodic restocking.
test_plan.observable_measure: Stockout count, excess inventory, and number of reorder events.
test_plan.success_signal: The proposed rule reduces stockouts without exceeding a predeclared excess-inventory threshold.
test_plan.failure_signal: Stockouts do not improve or excess inventory rises beyond the agreed limit.
test_plan.time_or_resource_limit: A small offline simulation with synthetic data; no real purchasing or user research.

rights_and_attribution.attribution_note: Synthetic example created for Friday schema and training tests; not a claim about a real historical, biological, or commercial system.

assessment.rationale: This is a synthetic schema demonstration. Its fictional source is unverified and cannot support a real-world analogy claim or retained-for-test decision.
